physics_goals.quote: The OPERA experiment was designed to search for νµ → ντ oscillations in appearance mode, i.e. by detecting the τ leptons produced in charged current ντ interactions.
physics_goals.value: Directly observe muon-neutrino to tau-neutrino oscillation in appearance mode over a long baseline

summary.plain: An experiment in a mountain tunnel in Italy that caught neutrinos fired 732 kilometres through the Earth from CERN in Switzerland. Its photographic-film-and-lead detector directly caught tau neutrinos appearing from a beam that started as muon neutrinos, proving they change type over the trip.
summary.technical: Emulsion-cloud-chamber (lead/nuclear-emulsion 'brick') experiment in LNGS Hall C, receiving the CNGS muon-neutrino beam from the CERN SPS over a 732 km baseline. Took data 2008-2012 and reported discovery of νμ → ντ appearance at 5.1σ significance from five candidate tau-neutrino interactions, confirming long-baseline neutrino oscillation in appearance mode.
